questions.q: What does the "Future Enterable" period status allow?
options: Both journal entry and posting
Journal entry, but not posting, since the period isn't actually open yet
Posting only, but not journal entry
Nothing at all, identical to Never Opened
questions.explain: Future Enterable allows pre-entering journals dated in an upcoming period, but posting is blocked until the period actually opens.

questions.q: Where does a controller change a period's status from Open to Closed?
options: Inquire on Detail Balances
The Chart of Accounts setup pages
Account Monitor
Manage Accounting Period, under General Accounting > Period Close
questions.explain: Manage Accounting Period is the page used to view and change a ledger's period statuses, including closing the current period.

questions.q: In the LTV Manufacturing Corporation example, what is required if an auditor finds a missing accrual in a period that has already closed?
options: Nothing — closed periods automatically absorb later corrections
Permanently closing the period immediately
Creating an entirely new ledger
Reopening the period, posting the correction, re-running dependent reports/consolidation, re-closing, and notifying anyone who used the original numbers
questions.explain: Reopening a closed period requires a full sequence of disruptive steps, which is why avoiding the need to reopen is the real goal of pre-close review.

questions.q: What makes "Permanently Closed" different from a regular "Closed" status?
options: There is no actual difference between the two
Permanently Closed periods allow new journal entry, Closed periods do not
A Closed period can still be reopened if needed; a Permanently Closed period cannot be reopened under any circumstances
Permanently Closed only applies to budget balances
questions.explain: Closed periods retain the option to be reopened; Permanently Closed is a final, one-way state applied once there's no remaining reason to post there.

questions.q: Why is changing a period's status to Closed typically the final action of the close checklist?
options: Because it happens automatically at the start of every period with no review
Because it must happen before reviewing any account balances
Because it is the formal declaration that the period's books are final, made only after unposted journals are cleared and reconciliation is complete
Because closing a period and reconciling subledgers are unrelated activities
questions.explain: Closing the period is the formal, final step, appropriately sequenced after the reconciliation and journal-clearing work described in lessons 33 and 34.
